module_summary: dash_widgets.c holds the dashboard's modal on-screen keyboard (pad and USB entry, filename/IP variants) and the worker-backed file/folder picker dashPickPath. dash_worker.c is the single background EE thread with a 32-entry job queue, status channel, IOP-reset parking handshake and the activity pill. draw.c, draw_gs.c and draw_text.c are the classic uLE gsKit drawing layer: header/message line, sprites and frames, GS mode setup and switching, the 8x16 font renderer, ELISA Shift-JIS rendering and SJIS-to-ASCII transcoding, all routed through the dashboard legacy theme when it is on. editor.c is the classic multi-window TextEditor main loop (pad/virtual keyboard input, drawing, tooltips); the dashboard uses dash_editor.c instead but the classic editor is still reachable from the classic filer and the Misc/TextEditor launch path.

reusable_helpers.name: dashWorkerSubmit
reusable_helpers.what: queue a run/done job pair on the background worker thread; done runs on the UI thread

reusable_helpers.name: dashWorkerAwait
reusable_helpers.what: wait for a worker job while animating, with optional cancel and a delayed loading overlay

reusable_helpers.name: dashWorkerStatus
reusable_helpers.what: semaphore-protected progress text and done/total counters written by jobs

reusable_helpers.name: dashPickPath
reusable_helpers.what: modal file/folder picker with device list, extension filter and worker-read listings

reusable_helpers.name: pickExtOk
reusable_helpers.what: match a filename against a '|' separated extension list, with 'NAME/' folder tokens

reusable_helpers.name: pickLastDirIs
reusable_helpers.what: case-insensitive test of the last folder name of a path

reusable_helpers.name: transcpy_sjis
reusable_helpers.what: convert a Shift-JIS save title to ASCII using two 256-entry lookup tables

reusable_helpers.name: is576pSupported
reusable_helpers.what: ROMVER based check for native 576p support

reusable_helpers.name: fadeScreenToBlack
reusable_helpers.what: 8-frame fade of the current GS frame to black before a handoff or mode switch

reusable_helpers.name: clearScreenToBlack
reusable_helpers.what: clear both GS framebuffers and BGCOLOR to black

findings.title: loadIcon is never called: TexIcon, FOLDER/WARNING and the whole of src/icon.c are dead with it
findings.problem: loadIcon appears only at its definition (draw.c:206) and prototype (launchelf.h:505). It is the only user of TexIcon (draw.c:15, launchelf.h:473) and of icon_folder/icon_warning, the two 1024-byte arrays that make up all 2055 lines of src/icon.c (compiled via ps2.yaml:559). The FOLDER/WARNING index macros (launchelf.h:466-467) are used nowhere. loadIcon would also free() static arrays if it ever ran.
findings.fix: Delete loadIcon, TexIcon, the FOLDER/WARNING macros, the icon_folder/icon_warning/TexIcon externs and the loadIcon prototype; delete src/icon.c and its ps2.yaml entry.
findings.benefit: ~2085 source lines removed (2055 of them a byte table). MEASURED: linker already discards .text.loadIcon (308 B) and icon.o .data (2048 B); TexIcon 80 B .bss stays in the shipped ELF (no -fdata-sections) and goes away.
findings.evidence: Grep -w loadIcon|TexIcon|icon_folder|icon_warning over the whole repo (src include tests scripts docs ps2.yaml): only draw.c:15,206-226, icon.c:2,1030, launchelf.h:469,470,473,505. Grep -w FOLDER|WARNING over *.c/*.h: only launchelf.h:466-467 plus unrelated string text. evidence/Launchstation/raw/link/wLaunchELF-gc-discarded-first-party.tsv lists draw.o .text.loadIcon 308 and icon.o .data 2048; raw/sizes/wLaunchELF-unstripped-all-symbols-by-size.tsv has TexIcon 80 .bss. No test references icon.c or loadIcon.

findings.title: Commented-out WriteFont_C font dumper in draw.c and its leftovers
findings.problem: WriteFont_C (a developer tool that dumps font_uLE as C source) exists only inside a /* */ block in draw.c, with a commented prototype in launchelf.h and a commented call in main_info_screens.c. No build can enable it without editing three files.
findings.fix: Delete the commented block, its banner, the commented prototype and the commented call.
findings.benefit: ~60 comment lines removed; no binary change (INFERRED: code is commented out).
findings.evidence: Grep WriteFont_C over the repo: draw.c:343,346,399 (inside the comment), launchelf.h:507-508 (comments), main_info_screens.c:303 (commented call). Nothing else.

findings.title: Orphan 'endfunc' banners and headings for functions that moved out of draw.c and editor.c
findings.problem: draw.c keeps empty banners for loadFont, drawChar, drawChar2, printXY, printXY_sjis and transcpy_sjis, which now live in draw_text.c. editor.c keeps 'ends menu', 'endfunc Virt_KeyBoard_Entry', 'endfunc KeyBoard_Entry' and 'ends Window_Selector' banners for code split into editor_menu.c/editor_input.c. dash_widgets.c:362-363 is a heading with no code under it.
findings.benefit: ~46 comment lines removed; no binary change.
findings.evidence: Read the cited ranges: comment lines only. Grep 'int loadFont|void drawChar|int printXY' finds the definitions in draw_text.c:67,107,142,159,206,333. editorMenu/editorSelectWindow are in editor_menu.c:6,139 and editorVirtualKeyboardEntry/editorKeyboardEntry in editor_input.c:169,428. Grep 'endfunc' in tests: only banners of filer_actions.c, filer_browser.c and init.c are used as slice markers, none of the cited ones.

findings.title: printXY_sjis repeats the Shift-JIS to ELISA index mapping and symbol table that dash_font.c also has
findings.problem: draw_text.c:266-292 converts SJIS to EUC and walks font404 to get the ELISA glyph index; dash_font.c:46-68 (elisaGlyphIndex, commented 'Same ... mapping as the classic renderer') does the same arithmetic. The five PlayStation-button codes (0x819B, 0x817E, 0x81A0, 0x81A2, 0x81A1) are hand-written as five copy-paste switch cases in draw_text.c:222-260 and again as an if-chain in dash_font.c:121-125.
findings.fix: Make elisaGlyphIndex non-static (or move it next to font404 in draw_text.c) and call it from printXY_sjis (glyph * 8 is the byte offset); replace the five switch cases with one small code-to-glyph table shared by both files.
findings.benefit: ~45 lines removed (INFERRED: 39 lines of switch cases become ~6, 27 lines of mapping become one call); a few hundred bytes of .text (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read draw_text.c:206-332 and dash_font.c:39-144. Both compute code -= 0x4000 for >=0xE000, the same lead/trail shuffle, +0xA1A1, row*94 and the font404 subtraction loop; dash_font adds a lead/trail validity check and bounds n < 55016/8, while draw_text bounds n*8 <= 55008 (same limit). printXY_sjis callers: filer_browser.c:1815. Check before merging: glyph range edge (55008 vs 55016) and the y+1 nudge for code <= 0x829A stay in printXY_sjis.

findings.title: editor.c: NEW and OPEN menu branches are copies, and the open-window count loop is written five times
findings.problem: The ret == NEW and ret == OPEN branches (270-292 and 293-316) are identical except for editorNew vs editorOpenFile and one drawMsg. The loop 'Num_Window = 0; for i < 10 if Window[i][OPENED] Num_Window++' appears at 271-275, 288-292, 295-299, 312-316 and 330-334, and the first-free-window search twice (277-282, 301-306).
findings.fix: Add one static countOpenWindows() and merge NEW/OPEN into one branch that picks editorNew or editorOpenFile.
findings.justification: The helper replaces five copies of the same loop and the merge removes a 23-line duplicate branch; net source shrinks.
findings.benefit: ~30 lines removed (INFERRED from cited ranges); small .text saving (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read editor.c:267-357 line by line. TextEditor is still called from filer_browser.c:1554 and main_actions.c:231,771, so the code is live.

findings.title: draw_gs.c: TV mode to GS mode mapping written twice, and updateScreenMode recomputes what applyGSParams sets
findings.problem: setupGS and updateScreenMode each contain a switch mapping TV_mode_* to GS_MODE_*. updateScreenMode then recomputes height/interlace/field from the GS mode with ternaries that restate the per-mode values already encoded in applyGSParams.
findings.fix: Use one static tvModeToGsMode() in both functions. tests/test_display_feedback.py:132 asserts the source contains 'case TV_mode_576P:' twice and must be updated with it.
findings.justification: One mapping function replaces two copies; net lines go down.
findings.benefit: ~14 lines removed (INFERRED from cited ranges); no measurable size change.
findings.evidence: Read draw_gs.c in full. tests/test_display_feedback.py:132 pins gs.count('case TV_mode_576P:') == 2; tests/test_r3z_video_switch.py and test_dashboard_present_buffers.py slice the source between 'void setupGS(void)' and 'void updateScreenMode(void)', so keep those signatures.

findings.title: loadFont closes a failed descriptor and seeks to 0 twice
findings.problem: When genOpen fails (fd < 0) loadFont still calls genClose(fd) on the negative value (line 76). Line 79 seeks to 0 on a freshly opened file right before seeking to the end, and line 84 seeks to 0 again.
findings.fix: Delete the genClose in the fd < 0 branch and the first genLseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET).
findings.benefit: 2 lines and two IO calls removed (INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Read draw_text.c:67-106. Callers: config_startup.c:131,173, config.c:1611, dash_settings.c:2128,2132,2565, main_actions.c:786, main_startup.c:708,716.

findings.title: dashPickPath: pickParent ignores its size argument and the 'go to parent' block is written twice
findings.problem: pickParent takes int size only to cast it to void (line 1084). Both callers (Back at 1164-1170, the Up row at 1218-1223) do the same four steps: copy pk.dir to a local buffer, pickParent, pickOpen, sel = 0.
findings.fix: Drop the size parameter and fold the copy + pickOpen into pickParent (pickUp), so both call sites become one call plus sel = 0.
findings.evidence: Grep pickParent over the repo: dash_widgets.c:1066 (definition), 1167, 1221 (calls); no test extracts it.

findings.title: visibleWork() in dash_worker.c only forwards to dashWorkerQueued(DASH_JOB_VISIBLE)
findings.problem: visibleWork is a one-line static wrapper with one caller (dash_worker.c:358).
findings.fix: Delete visibleWork and call dashWorkerQueued(DASH_JOB_VISIBLE) at line 358.
findings.benefit: 4 lines removed; no binary change (inlined already, INFERRED).
findings.evidence: Grep visibleWork: dash_worker.c:351 and :358 only. tests/test_worker_queue.py slices dash_worker.c only up to '// Waiting for results' (line 293), so it does not touch this function.
